title: Microsoft Teams: Teams Phone multi-line (several phone numbers per user)
summary: Hold: the emergency-location control pairs a configuration path with a read-only PowerShell command, which cannot set the location. The licensing, administrator-controlled default, rollout dates and documented limitations are supported.

claims.claim: Teams Phone multi-line lets administrators assign multiple phone numbers to one user.
claims.quote: Multi-line gives callers more flexibility and control by allowing administrators to assign more than one phone number to a single user.

claims.claim: Learn calls the additional numbers alternate lines.
claims.quote: Multi-line phone numbers are categorized as alternate line in Teams Phone and are additional phone numbers assigned to a user.

claims.claim: The user retains one Teams account for all assigned numbers.
claims.quote: Administrators can assign up to 11 phone numbers (including Primary line and Private line) to a single Teams Phone user, all within one Teams account.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Inbound calls to every assigned number ring the same user, including on Teams mobile.
claims.quote: All inbound PSTN calls to any assigned number ring the same user in Teams across Teams desktop, Teams web, Teams Phone devices, and Teams mobile (iOS/Android).

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: On supported clients users choose an outbound number through Call As or line-specific tabs.
claims.quote: Users can choose any assigned line for outbound calls via the Call As dropdown or line-specific tabs.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes assignment of up to 10 numbers per user.
claims.quote: allowing administrators to assign up to 10 phone numbers to a single user

claims.claim: MC1253752 describes assignment of up to 10 numbers per user.
claims.quote: Admins can assign up to 10 telephone numbers to a single Teams Phone user.

claims.claim: Learn gives a total limit of 11 numbers comprising one primary, one private and up to nine alternate numbers.
claims.quote: Assign up to 11 phone numbers (1 primary + 1 private + up to 9 alternate) to a single Teams user.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Users and licences
claims.claim: A user can have one primary line and up to nine alternate lines.
claims.quote: Users can be assigned one primary line and up to nine more alternate lines.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Users and licences
claims.claim: At most one Teams Phone Mobile number can be assigned to a user.
claims.quote: There can be a maximum of one Teams Phone Mobile number assigned to a single user.

claims.claim: Assigned numbers can be in different countries.
claims.quote: These numbers can be in different countries or use different PSTN connectivity types

claims.claim: Numbers can mix Calling Plan, Direct Routing, Operator Connect and Teams Phone Mobile connectivity.
claims.quote: any mix of Calling Plan (CP), Direct Routing (DR), Operator Connect (OC), and Teams Phone Mobile (maximum of one)

claims.claim: Each alternate number appears as a separate Calls app tab on desktop and web.
claims.quote: Teams for Windows, Mac, and web fully support multi-line calling. Each alternate number appears as a separate tab in the Calls app.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Cloud and platforms
claims.claim: Learn documents full multi-line calling support on Teams for Windows, Mac and web.
claims.quote: Teams for Windows, Mac, and web fully support multi-line calling.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Teams mobile outbound alternate-line selection is coming soon and is not currently supported.
claims.quote: Coming soon. Mobile app support for alternate lines is planned for a future update. For now, on Teams mobile (iOS/Android), alternate lines can receive inbound calls but cannot be selected for outbound calls or shown any multi-line options.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Each alternate number needs its own emergency location.
claims.quote: Assign an emergency location for the alternate number.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: An alternate number's emergency location must match its country for proper emergency call handling.
claims.quote: This location must match the alternate phone number's country location for proper emergency call handling.

claims.where: summary; controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Applicable number-level policies must be assigned to alternate numbers and do not fall back to user-level policies.
claims.quote: There are several phone number policies applicable to alternate lines. These policies must be set at number level and won't fall back to user assigned policies.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: All lines share the user's single voicemail box.
claims.quote: All lines share one voicemail box. Notifications don't indicate which number the caller dialed. No separate voicemail per line.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Voicemail notifications do not identify which number was dialled.
claims.quote: Notifications don't indicate which number the caller dialed.

claims.claim: Call history is unified across lines with identifiers showing the number used.
claims.quote: All calls from all lines appear in a single call history with identifiers showing which number was used.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Calling Line Identity policy controls outbound caller ID on individual alternate lines.
claims.quote: Calling Line Identity (Caller ID) Policy | Controls outbound caller ID masking or replacement for calls made on the alternate line.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Direct Routing alternate numbers require Online Voice Routing Policy.
claims.quote: Online Voice Routing Policy | Required for alternate phone numbers with Direct Routing.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Direct Routing alternate numbers require Emergency Call Routing Policy.
claims.quote: Emergency Call Routing Policy | Required for alternate phone numbers with Direct Routing.

claims.claim: Calls to and from Direct Routing numbers fail without a voice routing policy.
claims.quote: Without a voice routing policy, calls to and from Direct Routing numbers fail.

claims.claim: User call forwarding settings apply uniformly to primary and alternate lines.
claims.quote: User Call settings (forwarding, redirection) apply uniformly across primary and alternate lines.

claims.claim: Forwarding the primary line to a number or delegate forwards alternate-line calls to that same destination.
claims.quote: If a user forwards the primary line to any phone number or delegate, calls to alternate lines are also forwarded to same phone number or delegate.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Forwarding alternate-line calls can result in extra cost depending on licensing.
claims.quote: Call forwarding for alternate lines follows the same rules as primary line. If a user forwards the primary line to any phone number or delegate, calls to alternate lines are also forwarded to same phone number or delegate. Depending on licensing, this action may result in extra cost.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Alternate numbers cannot be added to call queues.
claims.quote: Alternate numbers are direct user lines only and can't be added to Call Queues or Auto Attendants.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Alternate numbers cannot be added to auto attendants.
claims.quote: Alternate numbers are direct user lines only and can't be added to Call Queues or Auto Attendants.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Per-line delegation is not yet supported.
claims.quote: Delegation and call groups apply uniformly; per-line delegation isn't supported yet.

claims.claim: Call groups do not yet have separate alternate-line support.
claims.quote: Call Delegation / Call Groups | Not yet supported. Delegation and call groups apply uniformly; per-line delegation isn't supported yet.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: System removal of the primary line also removes all alternate lines.
claims.quote: Removal of primary line also removes all alternate lines from the user. The primary line can be removed from the user by a system provisioning event

claims.claim: Licence removal can trigger system removal of the primary line.
claims.quote: The primary line can be removed from the user by a system provisioning event such as license removal

claims.claim: Phone number port-out can trigger system removal of the primary line.
claims.quote: The primary line can be removed from the user by a system provisioning event such as license removal, phone number port-out

claims.claim: Migration between number types can trigger system removal of the primary line.
claims.quote: The primary line can be removed from the user by a system provisioning event such as license removal, phone number port-out, phone number migration between number types

claims.claim: A primary usage-location change can trigger system removal of the primary line.
claims.quote: The primary line can be removed from the user by a system provisioning event such as license removal, phone number port-out, phone number migration between number types, and user's primary usage location change.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Manual unassignment requires removal of all alternate numbers before the primary number.
claims.quote: You can't unassign a user's primary phone number while they still have alternate phone numbers assigned. You must remove all alternate phone numbers first, then remove the primary number.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Changing an alternate number removes its assigned policies, which need reassignment.
claims.quote: When you change an alternate phone number, all policies previously assigned to that number are automatically removed. You'll need to reassign policies to the new number (as applicable) after the change.

claims.claim: Unassigning an alternate number removes its associated policies.
claims.quote: Unassigning or changing an alternate phone number removes all policies associated with that number.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Multi-line is not supported for users located in India.
claims.quote: User should not be located in India. We currently do not support multi-line in India.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope: Users and licences; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Users need an assigned primary line from their usage location before an alternate line can be assigned.
claims.quote: Users must have a primary line assigned from their usage location before an alternate line can be assigned.

claims.claim: Users must be voice enabled, with Enterprise Voice on, for alternate lines.
claims.quote: Users must be "voice enabled" for alternate lines. ... Under the Account tab > Assigned phone number, turn Enterprise Voice to On and select Save.

claims.claim: Configuration requires Teams Administrator, Teams Communications Administrator or Teams Telephony Administrator.
claims.quote: Admin role: You must have one of the following roles: Teams Administrator; Teams Communications Administrator; Teams Telephony Administrator

claims.claim: MC1253752 requires Teams Administrator or equivalent permissions for number assignment management.
claims.quote: Managing multi-line number assignments requires the Teams Administrator role (or equivalent permissions).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Alternate assignment with Set-CsPhoneNumberAssignment requires Teams PowerShell module 7.6.0 or later.
claims.quote: Alternate number assignment was introduced in Teams PowerShell module 7.6.0.

claims.claim: The Learn multi-line page publishes no separate alternate-line price or meter at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Phone multi-line alternate lines separate price meter billing charge. Opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/multi-line in full; it gives licensing requirements and a forwarding-cost caveat but no separate price or meter.

claims.claim: Alternate numbers are assigned through Teams admin center > Users > Manage users > user > Account tab > Assigned phone number > Assign alternate phone number.
claims.quote: From the Teams admin center, go to Users > Manage users. ... Select a user. ... From the user's Account tab, under Assigned phone number, select Assign alternate phone number.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Set-CsPhoneNumberAssignment -Identity <user> -TelephoneNumber <number> -NumberType <type> -AssignmentCategory Alternate assigns an alternate line.
claims.quote: Set-CsPhoneNumberAssignment -Identity user1@contoso.com -TelephoneNumber '+1555555555' -NumberType CallingPlan -LocationId "7fda0c0b-6a3d-48b8-854b-3fbe9dcf6513" -AssignmentCategory Alternate

claims.claim: Number policies are assigned through Teams admin center > Users > Manage users > user > Account tab > Assigned phone number > alternate number > Policies > Assign policy > Assign policies.
claims.quote: From the user's Account tab, find the alternate phone number you want to configure under Assigned phone number section. ... On the alternate number card, look at the Policies section: ... If no policies are assigned, you see Assign policy link. ... In the Assign policies panel

claims.claim: Set-CsPhoneNumberPolicyAssignment -TelephoneNumber <number> -PolicyType <policy type> -PolicyName <policy name> assigns number-level policies.
claims.quote: Number level policies can be assigned to alternate lines using Set-CsPhoneNumberPolicyAssignment cmdlet. ... Set-CsPhoneNumberPolicyAssignment -TelephoneNumber +14255551234 -PolicyType TenantDialPlan -PolicyName "HR Department Dial Plan"

claims.claim: Emergency locations are edited through Teams admin center > Voice > Phone Numbers > phone number > Edit > Assign/unassign > Emergency location.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Voice > Phone Numbers. ... Select the phone number in the list and then select Edit button at the top of the list to open Assign/unassign panel. ... Clear the Emergency location and select a new location.

claims.claim: Get-CsPhoneNumberAssignment -AssignedPstnTargetId <user> is the automation counterpart to the row's emergency-location configuration path.
claims.quote: This cmdlet displays information about one or more phone numbers. You can filter the phone numbers to return by using different parameters.
claims.fix: Keep this row for emergency-location configuration: change governs to 'Emergency locations assigned to alternate numbers', scope to 'other', api.call to 'Set-CsPhoneNumberAssignment -TelephoneNumber <number> -LocationId <location id>', and api.docs to 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csphonenumberassignment'. That reference states that -LocationId assigns the location to the phone number. Keep the existing UI path and Operator Connect caveat. Apply the same changes to the rendered row; do not add a row.

claims.claim: Dial Out Restriction (OnlineDialOutPolicy) cannot be assigned per number through Teams admin center and requires PowerShell.
claims.quote: Dial Out Restriction (OnlineDialOutPolicy) | Restricts outbound dialing permissions per number. This policy isn't available to be assigned via TAC. Use Teams PowerShell module.

claims.claim: Shared Call Routing Policy cannot be assigned per number through Teams admin center and requires PowerShell.
claims.quote: Shared Call Routing Policy | Enables assigning a soft phone number that uses Shared Calling for call routing. This policy isn't available to be assigned via TAC. Use Teams PowerShell module.

claims.claim: All seven available number-level policies can be assigned with Teams PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can assign all 7 available number level policies using Teams PowerShell Module.

claims.claim: PhoneNumber is an alias of the Set-CsPhoneNumberAssignment TelephoneNumber parameter.
claims.quote: ### -TelephoneNumber ... | Aliases: | PhoneNumber |

claims.claim: PhoneNumberType is an alias of the Set-CsPhoneNumberAssignment NumberType parameter.
claims.quote: ### -NumberType ... | Aliases: | PhoneNumberType |

claims.claim: Manage users has an Alternate phone number(s) column for reviewing users' alternate numbers.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Users > Manage users. ... Look for the Alternate phone number(s) column in the table.

claims.claim: Voice > Phone Numbers exposes an Assigned as column and an Alternate filter for alternate-number inventory.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Voice > Phone Numbers. ... You can use the Assigned as filter set to Alternate to narrow the list.

claims.claim: Ordinary users cannot assign alternate numbers themselves; assignment requires administrator permissions.
claims.quote: Admin role: You must have one of the following roles: Teams Administrator; Teams Communications Administrator; Teams Telephony Administrator

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Multi-line management through Graph API is not yet available.
claims.quote: Graph API | Not yet Supported. Multi-line management via Graph API isn't yet available; admins must use PowerShell or TAC to manage alternate phone numbers.

claims.claim: Native dialer support for an alternate Teams Phone Mobile number is planned with Teams mobile alternate-line support.
claims.quote: Teams Phone Mobile (SIM) First Run experience and native dialer support for alternate Teams Phone Mobile number isn't yet available. This feature is to be released along with support for Teams mobile (iOS/Android).

claims.claim: Assign policy appears when no number-level policies are assigned.
claims.quote: If no policies are assigned, you see Assign policy link. Select the link to assign new policies.

claims.claim: Setting or changing an Operator Connect emergency location depends on the operator, which administrators should contact for details.
claims.quote: If assigning Operator Connect numbers, the ability to set or change the emergency location depends on the operator. Contact the corresponding operator for more information.

Tenant Dial Plan is available as a number-level policy for alternate numbers.
claims.quote: The following policies support per-number assignment for alternate lines: ... Tenant Dial Plan | Controls number normalization rules for the specific alternate number.

claims.claim: Emergency Calling Policy is available as a number-level emergency policy for alternate numbers.
claims.quote: The following policies support per-number assignment for alternate lines: ... Emergency Calling Policy | Defines emergency calling notification and routing behavior per number.

claims.claim: Existing number-level policy assignments are changed through Edit policy and the Edit policies panel.
claims.quote: If policies are already assigned, you see Edit policy link. To assign new policies or update existing policies, select the link. ... In the Edit policies panel, select the desired policy from each dropdown menu.
